title: Negative binomial as a named overdispersed-count cousin
dek: Wikipedia NB: extra-Poisson variance. stats-overdispersion and stats-poisson already own the TB-count lecture.
story: Negative binomial on Wikipedia is a count distribution with a variance larger than the mean, often written as a Poisson–gamma mixture. It is the named cousin when colony counts or incident-case tallies refuse Poisson marriage.
stats-overdispersion already says when to leave Poisson. stats-quasi-likelihood keeps V(μ)=φμ without a full NB density. This card is the encyclopedia random component.
NB-1 versus NB-2 variance functions are a software fork; say which.
deep: If the extra variance is a few huge outliers, NB still may be the wrong story (robustness).
Zero-inflation is another extra story, not automatic NB.
A GLM with NB random component still needs a link and a linear predictor (wiki-glm).
Do not 'fix' overdispersion by deleting the interesting high-count lineage.

visual.caption: Mean held, variance grows: Poisson versus NB. Teaching bars, not a fitted dataset.
